text:
incidents-bot: ALERT: gpu-queue-alert: queue depth for inference-gpu-pool exceeded threshold (1200 requests, >300s avg wait). Autoscaler reported repeated failures to add GPU capacity. Paging oncall. https://internal.ops/alerts/1762345678 :siren:

maria g: I'm on it, grabbing brief. Which cluster?

sanjay r: aws-prod-gpu-cluster in us-west-2. We're seeing steady queue growth and token throttling for hosted API.

kevin l: I'm seeing a spike in errors from the router: 503 /model/generate -> "no healthy backends" for several routes. Customers complaining about timeouts.

maria g: Pulling autoscaler logs now.

maria g: ```
2026-06-12T14:02:11Z cluster-autoscaler: scale up: attempt to increase size of nodegroup gpu-nodegroup-1 (min:2 max:10)
2026-06-12T14:02:11Z cluster-autoscaler: unable to scale up: failed to create instance: LaunchTemplateMismatch: launch template id does not match nodegroup config
2026-06-12T14:02:12Z cluster-autoscaler: failed to increase ASG size: AccessDenied: iam:PassRole
```

taylor oncall: AccessDenied for iam:PassRole suggests the autoscaler role or nodegroup role lost permission to pass the instance profile. Could be a drift in the nodegroup launch template or an IAM policy change from this morning's infra rollout.

ops-bot: Deploy job #1956 (infra/launch-templates) completed at 13:47 UTC targeting us-west-2 (change-id: lt-2026-06-12-13).

kevin l: That matches — infra pushed a new LT earlier. If the autoscaler/ASG are still pointing to the old template arn, AWS will refuse to use the new profile or there can be mismatch errors.

sanjay r: Quick triage plan: 1) try a manual scale with updated launch template; 2) if that fails, create a fallback nodegroup with a permissive launch template and instance profile; 3) enable routing fallback to CPU-only pool for non-latency models to reduce pressure.

maria g: Attempting manual ASG update to set LaunchTemplate to latest and increase desired capacity to +3 now (console). Will report status.

maria g: Manual update failed via API: AccessDenied: You do not have permission to perform "ec2:RunInstances" with the target profile.

kevin l: Looks like the instance profile used by ASG/cluster-autoscaler can't be passed by the autoscaler role. We need iam:PassRole on role arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/redwood-autoscaler-role.

taylor oncall: Can infra restore iam:PassRole for the autoscaler role? @ops-bot can you roll back the LT change or at least reapply iam:PassRole?

ops-bot: @taylor oncall @kevin l Noted. Creating infra incident and page infra oncall. Rollback is nontrivial during creation window but we can apply additional iam:PassRole binding to the autoscaler role. Starting now. Change window ETA ~10m.

csm-laura: Customers impacted: several mid-market customers reported elevated 504s and degraded throughput. CS has flagged 3 active support tickets (high). We're placing a banner on status.redwoodai.com.

maria g: Meanwhile, to reduce immediate pressure, I changed routing to favor smaller models and enabled prefix caching on the most common prompt buckets. That dropped queue delta by ~18%.

sanjay r: Also starting a temporary remediation: create an emergency GPU nodegroup using an older known-good launch template and a node IAM profile we control. I'm running an eksctl create nodegroup command.

sanjay r: ```
eksctl create nodegroup --cluster aws-prod-gpu-cluster --name gpu-ephemeral-1 --node-type p4d.24xlarge --nodes 2 --nodes-min 2 --nodes-max 6 --node-ami auto --node-labels=preemptible=true --asg-access
```

maria g: That returned: "Error: failed to create nodegroup: AccessDenied: iam:CreateInstanceProfile". Looks like broader IAM protections applied during infra rollout are blocking instance profile operations from our deploy service account.

kevin l: OK, infra has the keys. Infra oncall says they're applying iam:PassRole and instance profile create perms for the autoscaler service account and the deploy account. They estimate 8-12 minutes.

ops-bot: infra-oncall paged. Change request CR-6942 submitted.

taylor oncall: While infra fixes IAM, we should switch a subset of traffic to Dedicated capacity or Dedicated fallbacks to keep paying customers alive. @csm-laura can we identify the highest-risk customers and move them manually to dedicated endpoints / allocated pools?

csm-laura: Yes, pushing a manual migration for 2 enterprise customers who have dedicated Dedicated pools; contacting legal & AMs now. ETA 15m.

maria g: Autoscaler logs are showing repeated taint errors too: new nodes launched are getting tainted gpu-unavailable:NoSchedule by a node-init script because GPU drivers failed to initialize on that LT.

maria g: ```
kubelet[1234]: node "ip-10-0-12-34.us-west-2.compute.internal" had taint added: gpu-unavailable:NoSchedule
systemd[1]: nvidia-driver.service: failed to start
```

kevin l: So even if IAM is fixed, the launch template might be referencing a newer AM or driver combination that breaks driver install path. We need to ensure the launch template's user-data and AM are correct.

sanjay r: Proposed next steps: (A) infra applies iam:PassRole so autoscaler can pass roles; (B) if autoscaler still can't scale, infra will temporarily increase ASG max for gpu-nodegroup-1 and attach the known-good LT; (C) we create ephemeral nodegroup with fallback AM; (D) routing fallback to CPU for non-critical models.

maria g: Infra confirmed iam:PassRole applied at 14:18 UTC. Autoscaler re-attempting scale now.

maria g: ```
2026-06-12T14:19:05Z cluster-autoscaler: scale up: requested 3 nodes for gpu-nodegroup-1
2026-06-12T14:19:23Z cluster-autoscaler: created 2 nodes; 1 failed due to driver init.
```

taylor oncall: Good progress. Kevin, can you cordon any nodes with the gpu-unavailable taint and mark for remediate (we don't want pods scheduled there)?

kevin l: Doing: `kubectl get nodes -l 'taint=gpu-unavailable' -o name | xargs kubectl cordon`

kevin l: Also draining one of the failed nodes to let daemonset retries reinstall driver: `kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

maria g: Queue backlog dropped from 1200 -> 420 after the two successful nodes and routing changes. Token throttling decreased but still degradation for some customers.

csm-laura: Status page update posted, and CS notified top customers. We're offering temporary capacity credits for impacted intervals.

taylor oncall: Handoff to next oncall @kevin l at 14:30 UTC. I'll be available on-call-runbook channel if anything regresses. Please capture post-incident notes and root cause hypotheses.

kevin l: Taking over. Current state: partial capacity restored (2 new nodes healthy), autoscaler now able to create nodes but launch template id drift + driver init issue remains for 1 node. IAM change applied. Queue at ~380 and falling. Customers triaged.

maria g: Filed an infra bug: LT-compatibility + AM-driver-mismatch. Also adding an action to add unit test to infra pipeline to prevent future LT/AM mismatches.

sanjay r: Follow-ups: 1) revert problematic LT or align nodegroup to the tested LT; 2) add policy to ensure deploy and autoscaler roles retain iam:PassRole across infra changes; 3) run canaries for driver install on new LT before rollout; 4) document manual fallback steps in runbook.

kevin l: I'll create the incident postmortem doc and tag infra/product/ops. Posting initial summary to #postmortems and scheduling RCA 48h.

csm-laura: Customers want timeline and compensation details; I'll coordinate with finance and AMs.

ops-bot: Incident resolved? Condition: queue < 300 AND error-rate reduced by >75% for 10m. Monitoring checks passing at 14:49 UTC.

kevin l: Marking incident as mitigated at 14:49 UTC. Leaving follow-ups open. Great work team. :tada:
